english.title: Fail to comply with initial notification requirements under domestic abuse protection order
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having been made the subject of a domestic abuse protection order on **(..SPECIFY DATE ORDER MADE..) by **(..SPECIFY COURT..), failed, without reasonable excuse, to notify the police of the matters required by section 41 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, namely

(A)_[name]_
(B)_[name and home address]_
(C)_[each of your names]_
(D)_[home address]_
(E)_[each of your names and your home address]_

within the period of three days beginning on the day on which the order was made
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 41(2) and 43(1)(a) and (3) of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021.

english.notes:
(i) This offence only applies in relation to domestic abuse protection orders (DAPOs) made within pilot areas, in the specified period -
(a) in the London boroughs of Bromley, Croydon and Sutton and the Metropolitan District of Greater Manchester for the period beginning with 27th November 2024, see the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 (Commencement No. 6 and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2024;
(b) in the non-metropolitan county of Cleveland for the period beginning with 5th March 2025, see the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 (Commencement No. 7 and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2025; and (c) in the non-metropolitan districts of Hartlepool, Middlesborough, Redcar and Cleveland and Stockton-on-Tees for the period beginning with 11th March, see the Domestic Abuse Act 2021 (Commencement No. 8 and Saving Provisions) Regulations 2025. The pilot ends on the 26th November 2025.
(ii) For further details on the pilot see the notes on section 27 of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021.
(iii) As per section 43(4), (5) and (6) of the Domestic Abuse Act 2021, a person commits this offence on the day on which the person first fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with a requirement imposed by or under section 41. The person continues to commit the offence throughout any period during which the failure continues. But the person may not be prosecuted more than once in respect of the same failure.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.
